# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)

concurrency:

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded

# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov

#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate

#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)

#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is

concurrency:

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)

#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage

#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)

#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not

arguments.content:
### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD CFG[providerTimeouts config + registry entries] --> RES[explicitStreamIdleForModel
entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov

#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)

{"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite).

entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

concurrency:

  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,

{"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD CFG[providerTimeouts config + registry entries] --> RES[explicitStreamIdleForModel
entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate

{"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite).

connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)

A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; #   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage

A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never

{"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; {"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD CFG[providerTimeouts config + registry entries] --> RES[explicitStreamIdleForModel
entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

{"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with
#                no commits since the last v* tag skips the whole gate

{"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD CFG[providerTimeouts config + registry entries] --> RES[explicitStreamIdleForModel
entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

{"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; # Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; PATH-TRIGGERED on pull_request events and SM
#               validation dispatches alike — the changes classifier
#               derives the validated diff via merge-base(origin/main,
#               HEAD) under dispatch-only CI; gh-1538 retired the
#               nightly full-suite macOS backstop, so this pre-merge leg
#               is the only macOS test surface)
#   flutter-app-lock-smoke → linux+windows flutter_app RELEASE builds,
#               run only when the diff modifies flutter_app/pubspec.lock
#               (issue #1267 N2; same path-triggered model — PRs not
#               touching the lockfile pay nothing)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
#   release-pending → gh-1551 empty-tick short-circuit: the schedule is
#                the release arming mechanism (gh-1537), but a tick with

{"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD CFG[providerTimeouts config + registry entries] --> RES[explicitStreamIdleForModel
entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

{"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; {"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; {"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite).

connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

{"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; {"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD CFG[providerTimeouts config + registry entries] --> RES[explicitStreamIdleForModel
entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```

A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; {"content":"### What changed The run-idle watchdog now derives its patience from the gh-1554 `providerTimeouts` precedence instead of a hardcoded 8-minute floor: `window = max(floor, effective streamIdleTimeoutMs)` where effective follows entry override (model-scoped / tuning-registry) > global section > floor. A warming-up model (self-hosted llama.cpp) gets exactly the patience the user configured; the zero-byte replay budget is additionally bounded by an explicitly configured `connectTimeoutMs`. ### Key decisions - **Read, don't rebuild, the gh-1554 precedence**: new pure helpers `explicitStreamIdleForModel` / `explicitConnectForModel` in `provider_tuning.dart` resolve the model-scoped window first, then the per-URL tuning registry, then the global section; the built-in 5-minute provider default is deliberately NOT a result, so unset config keeps today's behavior byte-for-byte (AC3). - **Window re-derives on every watchdog arm** (`Agent.runIdleWindow`): a mid-run roles failover re-windows around the model actually being streamed (AC2), and a config re-seed applies from the next arm (E3, no live re-arm). - **Replay bound** (`zeroByteAttemptBudget`, AC4/I2): no connect budget → the ladder's 2-attempt bound stands; a configured budget buys `1 + budget ~/ window` clamped to `[1, 2]` — a budget below the window stops the replay and the terminal names both values. - **Naming surfaces** (AC5): the watchdog fire, the zero-byte terminal, the replay notice, and the TUI stall banner all name the governing window + its precedence source and suggest raising `providerTimeouts.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; the stall notice keeps its early 2m UX ceiling (`min(ceiling, window)`, open question 1's sketched default). - E1 documented in the ladder: the killed request is aborted via the cancel token and its zero-byte partial dropped before any replay; billing dedup stays provider-side. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/run_idle_watchdog_window_test.dart \ test/agent/run_idle_watchdog_provider_window_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_stall_window_notice_test.dart \ test/providers/transient_retry_zero_byte_test.dart ``` AC1 (configured-window survival), AC2 (entry override wins per URL), AC3 (default parity: 2 kills → `(zero-byte stall)` abort unchanged), AC4 (connect-budget stop naming both values), AC5 (window + source on fire/terminal/notice/banner) are each covered; REG-1 rides the existing path-classified `test-core` CI leg (any `lib/` diff runs the full `dart test` suite).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD CFG[providerTimeouts config + registry entries] --> RES[explicitStreamIdleForModel
entry > registry > global] RES --> W[max runIdleTimeout floor, effective idle] W --> AGENT[Agent._armRunWatchdog] AGENT -->|fire names window + source| LADDER[transient ladder replay] LADDER -->|zero-byte kills| BUDGET[zeroByteAttemptBudget
connect budget bound] BUDGET -->|stop| TERM[terminal names window, source, budget] W --> CLI[TUI stall banner: min 2m notice, window naming] ```
